draft: Last week, our class visited the public library to learn how local records are stored. The librarian showed us several folders and explained how the catalogue works. We collected information about three streets and recorded the dates beside each note. My group compared two maps from different years. We noticed that some buildings had changed, but we did not know why. We decided to describe only the changes that we could see in the maps. After lunch, I checked our notes carefully with another student. We kept the original dates because they were important to the comparison. The final page included a short description of our visit and a list of the materials we had used. We did not claim that our small activity explained the history of the whole town. In our next lesson, we will ask the librarian about one street whose name appears differently in the two records. I enjoyed this activity because it gave me a reason to read local documents. It also reminded me to separate what I observed from what I only guessed. Our teacher asked us to keep both versions of our notes so that we could explain each change during the next class.

academicChecks.why: 文中只是陈述一次实地活动、记录方式和个人体验，没有把未经核实的信息当作普遍结论，也没有无依据的因果断言。
全文中心始终围绕一次图书馆活动、记录比较和后续提问展开，论题一致。
前句写“我们收集三条街的信息并记录日期”，后句接着写“小组比较不同年份的两张地图”，是同一活动流程中的自然推进，没有主题跳转。
